problem_statement: realstoman/nextjs-tailwindcss-portfolio is a runnable Next.js and Tailwind CSS personal portfolio for the designer Stoman: a home page with a hero banner and a projects portfolio grid, a full projects listing page, per-project detail pages, an about page, and a contact page, with a shared header (light and dark theme toggle) and footer, framer-motion transitions, and a local GeneralSans font. Above each project grid the site shows its own 'Filter work by category' control: a row of category tabs (All, Web Application, Mobile Application, UI/UX Design) derived from the six projects' own category field, plus a live result-count readout in the form 'Showing 2 of 6 . Web Application'. Clicking a category tab is meant to re-render the grid to the matching category and update the readout to match the cards shown. The same filter bar rides both the home route and the /projects listing so the browsing control stays continuous across the portfolio. In the current codebase this filter is broken three ways: (1) the category tab row is pinned to a fixed non-wrapping width, so at a 390px mobile width the tab row runs wider than the viewport and pushes the whole home document into horizontal overflow; (2) the filter bar is only mounted on the home route, so the /projects listing loses the shared 'Filter work by category' control entirely; (3) clicking a category tab flips the active-tab styling but the grid and the count readout never update, so the readout stays frozen on 'Showing all 6 projects' while every card remains visible, and the selected tab is rendered illegibly (near-white text on a near-white chip) with the filtered cards collapsing into an overlapping, clipped row. Repair the category filter so: the tab row wraps and introduces no new horizontal overflow at 390px; the 'Filter work by category' bar appears on both the home route and the /projects listing; clicking a category tab actually filters the grid and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 . <Category>' matching the cards shown; the active tab is legible; and the filtered cards render in a clean responsive grid. Keep the hero banner, the projects, the shared header and footer, the About counters and bio, and the project detail pages exactly as they are.
required_content: The 'Filter work by category' bar renders its category tabs (All, Web Application, Mobile Application, UI/UX Design) and its live result-count readout on the home page above the projects portfolio grid.
The same 'Filter work by category' bar also appears above the grid on the /projects listing page, so the browsing control is continuous across the portfolio (not home-only).

Clicking a category tab filters the project grid to that category and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 . <Category>' that matches the number of cards actually shown; clicking All restores all six.
The selected category tab is legible (clear contrast against its chip) and the filtered cards render in a clean responsive grid without overlapping or clipping.
At a 390px mobile viewport the home page has no new horizontal overflow: the category tab row wraps within the content column instead of forcing the document wider than the screen.
The hero banner, the six projects, the About page counters and bio, the per-project detail page, and the shared themed header and footer all stay intact and readable across pages.
design_constraints: Treat this as a repair of the portfolio's own project-grid category filter, not a redesign, rebrand, framework migration, or replacement portfolio.
Use the current visual vocabulary: light and dark Tailwind surfaces, indigo accents, ternary and gray text hierarchy, rounded pill tabs, subtle shadows, and the local GeneralSans font.
Keep the filter bar aligned to the existing centered container width and subordinate to the hero and the 'Projects portfolio' heading; do not turn it into a new marketing hero.

Do not introduce unrelated images, decorative gradients, or new copy; the intended change is the responsive layout, cross-route presence, legibility, and live filtering behavior of the category filter.
Keep the category tabs and cards inside the content column and avoid any new horizontal overflow of the document at 390px width.
The category labels, the readout format, the project cards, and the surrounding page DOM must stay consistent across viewports; the filter must actually re-derive its results from the selected tab.
state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home, and mobile_home capture the home page with the 'Filter work by category' bar above the projects portfolio grid; desktop and tablet fit, mobile at 390px currently overflows horizontally in the baseline.
desktop_projects captures the /projects listing; the reference shows the shared 'Filter work by category' bar there, while the defective legs drop it (cross-route regression).

desktop_filter_web captures the home page AFTER clicking the Web Application category tab: the reference shows 'Showing 2 of 6 . Web Application' with the two web cards in a clean grid; the defective leg leaves the readout frozen on 'Showing all 6 projects' with all cards overlapping.

desktop_about and desktop_project confirm the About counters and bio and the per-project detail content stay intact, and source inspection confirms components/projects/ProjectsGrid.jsx mounts the category filter over data/projectsData.js on both pages/index.jsx and pages/projects/index.jsx.

change_completion: Clicking a category tab filters the grid and the readout updates to 'Showing N of 6 . <Category>' matching the shown cards.
The 'Filter work by category' bar appears on both the home page and the /projects listing using concrete rendered text.
The repair keeps the six real projects and their categories rather than placeholder content.
design_consistency: The filter bar keeps the existing Tailwind portfolio shell, indigo accents, rounded pill tabs, and font rhythm.
The active tab is legible and the control stays subordinate to the hero and the projects grid rather than becoming a marketing hero.
regression: The hero banner, projects grid, About counters and bio, project detail content, and shared header and footer remain visible.
Project routing and the theme toggle behavior remain intact.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and mobile home states remain readable without new horizontal overflow.
The category tab row wraps cleanly at 390px and does not obscure the projects grid.
Desktop and tablet keep the comfortable single-row tab layout.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js + Tailwind portfolio repair/design-continuity task built on the portfolio's OWN project-grid category filter (components/projects/ProjectsGrid.jsx over data/projectsData.js), the native place this genre hosts a filter. The reference, baseline, and bad legs share byte-identical hero, projects, and site DOM; the leg-varying files are components/projects/ProjectsGrid.jsx (live vs frozen filter wiring), components/projects/projfilter.module.css (fluid wrapping tab row + clean responsive card grid vs fixed-width non-wrapping row and overlapping clipped grid), and data/projfilterRoutes.js (the cross-route presence whitelist). The reference passes all four gates. The baseline keeps the filter wiring live (so it passes the interaction gate) but pins the tab row to a fixed 560px non-wrapping width (mobile horizontal overflow and header-layout regression) and mounts the bar on the home route only (cross-page regression on /projects). The known-bad solution snapshots the filtered set and the count readout once at mount so the category click never re-filters (stale interaction), collapses the filtered cards into an overlapping clipped row, and renders the active tab illegibly, in addition to the fixed-width mobile overflow and the home-only mount. The four orthogonal discriminators are no_horizontal_overflow (mobile), visual_regression (desktop_filter_web), dom_assertions (the filter bar across the home and /projects routes), and interaction_assertions (the category tab re-derives the count). Screenshots for the home page, the /projects listing, and the About page are captured; each renders real portfolio imagery.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable Next.js + Tailwind personal portfolio (nextjs-tailwindcss-portfolio) whose project grid already ships a category filter over real project data; a repair/design-continuity task upgrades that native filter into a legible, cross-route, live category tab bar with a result count, giving four orthogonal deterministic discriminators.
